mainTopic: סוכה decorations, and when a כילה or canopy counts as a separate tent (for סוכה and for קריאת שמע)
overview: The amud opens at the end of a ברייתא that seems to support decorating a סוכה with sheets, but the גמרא rejects the proof because the sheets may have hung on the walls. It then rules that decorations hanging from the סכך do not reduce the סוכה's size, and רב אשי adds that decorations on the side do. A story about רב אשי's servant מנימין shows that even a drying shirt on the סוכה must come down once it could look like סכך that can become טמא. רב נחמן argues with רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא about decorations hanging four טפחים below the סכך. When רב נחמן hosts them in such a סוכה, they explain that they were exempt as שלוחי מצוה, so they never took back their ruling. Next, שמואל allows sleeping under a כילה in the סוכה if it is under ten טפחים, and the גמרא defends this against several challenges. Along the way it learns that fixed קינופות count as a tent even when low. The amud ends with שמואל's ruling about reciting קריאת שמע with one's head outside a כילה, which the גמרא limits to a כילה lower than ten טפחים.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: decorations stay until after the festival unless he made a condition
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא about decorating a סוכה with sheets finishes. You may not take anything from the decorations until the festival ends, unless you made a תנאי beforehand.
steps.simpleTranslation: …until the end of the last day of the festival. And if he made a condition about them, everything follows his condition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא that says a person may decorate his סוכה with sheets. This seems to prove that sheets under the סכך do not make the סוכה פסולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the previous amud, רב חסדא ruled that the משנה's פסולה applies only to a sheet spread under the סכך to catch falling leaves. A sheet spread there for decoration leaves the סוכה כשרה. This ברייתא is offered as support for him, because it treats decorative sheets as normal and only asks when you may use them. The point about a תנאי tells us that decorations are set aside for the מצוה for the whole festival unless you clearly said otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: The end of the festival day (after nightfall)

phrases.aramaic: עַד מוֹצָאֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל חַג.
phrases.english: until the conclusion of the last festival day of the Festival.
phrases.notes: Tail end of the ברייתא: one may not use the decorations until then.

phrases.english: And if he stipulated regarding them —
phrases.notes: He said beforehand that he is not fully setting them aside.

phrases.english: everything is according to his stipulation.
phrases.notes: He may use them as he stipulated.

steps.triggerLanguage: עד מוצאי יום טוב האחרון של חג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא begun on the previous amud. It is brought as support for the ruling that a sheet spread under the סכך for decoration does not make the סוכה פסולה.
steps.raayaObject: That decorative sheets may be spread in a סוכה without making it פסולה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about decorating a סוכה with sheets and other ornaments

steps.title: Rejection: maybe the sheets were hung on the side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא may mean sheets hung on the walls, not under the סכך.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps the sheets were on the side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and says the ברייתא proves nothing. The sheets it describes may have been hung on the walls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sheet on a wall does not stand between the person and the סכך, so it causes no problem. Only a sheet spread under the roofing could block the סכך. Since the ברייתא could be talking about wall sheets, it cannot serve as support for allowing decorative sheets under the סכך. That ruling has to stand without this proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps / maybe (a common way to reject a proof)
On the side (on the walls, not under the roof)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying decorations are bad. It only says this ברייתא cannot prove that sheets under the סכך are allowed.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is on the side.
phrases.notes: The sheets were spread on the walls, not beneath the סכך.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the ברייתא in step 1 by reading it as a different case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely. The ברייתא can be read as dealing with a different case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the sheets were under the סכך, but they may have been on the walls.

steps.title: סוכה decorations do not reduce the size of the סוכה
steps.stepSummary: A new ruling about decorations: they do not count as reducing the סוכה's measurements.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: סוכה decorations do not diminish the סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the topic is decorations, the גמרא brings a new ruling. Decorations hanging in the סוכה do not count as making it smaller.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Take a סוכה whose סכך is higher than twenty אמות, which is too high. Decorations hanging down from the סכך do not count as a new 'ceiling' that brings it within the allowed height. Decorations are treated as part of the סוכה's beauty, not as part of its structure.

phrases.english: It was stated: Sukkah decorations
phrases.notes: A new teaching connected to the topic of decorations.

phrases.english: do not diminish the sukkah.
phrases.notes: They do not lower the height of the סוכה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אתמר נויי סוכה אין ממעטין בסוכה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching on a related theme. The link is the word 'decorations'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Decorations hanging from the סכך do not count toward reducing the height of the סוכה.

steps.title: רב אשי: decorations on the side do reduce the סוכה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי adds a limit: decorations on the side do count and do reduce the סוכה's measurements.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: And from the side, they do diminish.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי qualifies the rule from step 3. Decorations placed on the side are treated differently from those hanging from the סכך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Decorations hanging from the סכך are treated as ornament and are ignored for measuring. Decorations on the side are treated as part of the structure. They therefore reduce the inner space, and if they bring it below seven by seven טפחים, the סוכה is פסולה.
steps.whatToRemember: Decorations hanging down from the סכך do not reduce the סוכה's size. Decorations on the side do.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
And from the side — they diminish.
phrases.notes: Side decorations count as part of the structure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב אשי ומן הצד ממעטין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the general rule in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Decorations placed on the side are counted and do reduce the סוכה's measurements.

steps.title: רב אשי tells his servant to take his drying shirt off the סוכה
steps.stepSummary: מנימין spread his wet shirt on top of the סוכה. רב אשי told him to take it down so people would not think the סוכה was roofed with something that can become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: מנימין, רב אשי's servant: his shirt got wet in water, and he spread it on the סוכה. רב אשי said to him: Take it down, so that people will not say they are roofing with an item that receives impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about רב אשי and his servant. רב אשי worried that a shirt lying on the סוכה would make onlookers think clothing was being used as סכך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clothing can become טמא, and anything that can become טמא may not be used as סכך. The shirt itself was not meant as סכך, but רב אשי worried about how it looked. People might draw the wrong conclusion about the halacha.

keyTerms.meaning: Lift it up / take it down
An item that can become ritually impure (not allowed as סכך)

phrases.english: Minyamin, the servant of Rav Ashi —
phrases.notes: Introduces the story.

phrases.english: his shirt became soaked in water,
and he spread it out on the sukkah.
phrases.notes: To dry it.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to him: Take it down,
so that they will not say that they are roofing
phrases.notes: A concern about appearances.

phrases.english: with an item that is susceptible to ritual impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story connected by theme: things placed on a סוכה that are not real סכך.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not leave clothing on top of a סוכה where people might mistake it for סכך.

steps.title: The servant objects: people can see the shirt is wet
steps.stepSummary: מנימין argues that nobody will be misled, because everyone can see the shirt is wet and is only drying.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they see that it is wet!
steps.whatsHappening: The servant challenges רב אשי's concern. Anyone looking can tell the shirt was put there only to dry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is aimed at the reason for the rule, which is how things look. If the reason a garment is lying there is obvious, there should be nothing to worry about.

phrases.english: But they see that it is wet!
phrases.notes: So no one will think it is סכך.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason רב אשי gave in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's concern that people will think the shirt is סכך
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: While the shirt is wet, everyone understands it is drying, so no one will be misled.

steps.title: רב אשי: I mean once it dries
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that his concern is for later, once the shirt is dry and people can no longer tell why it is there.
steps.simpleTranslation: I am telling you about when it becomes dry.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the servant. The problem is not now, while the shirt is wet, but later, once it is dry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the shirt is wet, its purpose is clear. Once it dries and stays on the סוכה, it looks like part of the roofing. So the shirt should be taken down by the time it dries.

phrases.english: Once it dries — that is what I am telling you.
phrases.notes: Take it down once it is dry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 6 by narrowing when רב אשי's rule applies.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the rule applies to a later time
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אשי's concern seemed to apply right away, while the shirt was obviously wet.
steps.terutzMaskana: The concern applies once the shirt is dry, when it can be mistaken for סכך.
steps.whatToRemember: Even something put on a סוכה for an innocent reason must be removed once it might look like סכך that can become טמא.

steps.title: Dispute: decorations hanging four טפחים below the סכך
steps.stepSummary: The אמוראים argue about decorations hanging four טפחים below the סכך. רב נחמן says the סוכה is כשרה. רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא say it is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: סוכה decorations that are distanced four handbreadths from it — רב נחמן said: It is fit. רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא said: It is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new dispute. The question is whether decorations hanging four טפחים below the סכך make the סוכה פסולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Four טפחים is a significant gap. Hanging that far below the סכך, the decorations might be treated as a separate covering between the person and the סכך. רב נחמן holds that decorations always belong to the סוכה and do not block. רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא hold that at that distance they do block, making the סוכה פסולה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next part of the sugya. The next steps tell a story in which the two sides of this very dispute meet in exactly such a סוכה.

phrases.english: It was stated: Sukkah decorations
that are distanced from it four handbreadths,
phrases.notes: Hanging four טפחים below the סכך.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: It is fit,

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: Rav Chisda and Rabba bar Rav Huna
say: It is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אתמר נויי סוכה המופלגין ממנה ארבעה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new dispute about decorations, separate from the story in steps 5 to 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dispute. רב נחמן says decorations four טפחים below the סכך leave the סוכה כשרה. רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא say they make it פסולה.

steps.title: רב נחמן hosts his opponents in a סוכה they consider invalid
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא visit the ריש גלותא. רב נחמן puts them in a סוכה with decorations hanging four טפחים below the סכך, and they say nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא happened to come to the house of the ריש גלותא. רב נחמן lodged them in a סוכה whose decorations hung four טפחים away from the roofing. They were silent and did not say anything to him at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about the very argument from Step 8. רב נחמן, who says such a סוכה is כשרה, puts the two rabbis who say it is פסולה into exactly that kind of סוכה, and they say nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story sets up a test. Their silence could mean they agree with רב נחמן after all. The next steps explain what their silence really meant.

keyTerms.meaning: the Exilarch, leader of the Jews in Bavel
he lodged them / gave them a place to stay

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: Rav Chisda and Rabba bar Rav Huna
happened to come to the house of the Exilarch.
Rav Nachman lodged them in a sukkah
phrases.notes: רב נחמן ran the Exilarch's household.

phrases.english: whose decorations hung four handbreadths away from it (the roofing),
phrases.notes: This is exactly the case argued about in Step 8.

phrases.aramaic: אִשְׁתִּיקוּ וְלָא אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ וְלָא מִידֵּי.
phrases.english: they were silent and said nothing at all to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אִיקְּלַעוּ לְבֵי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts the argument from Step 8 into a real-life situation where the two sides meet.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A story: the rabbis who hold the סוכה is פסולה are placed in such a סוכה and stay silent.

steps.title: רב נחמן asks if they changed their minds
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks whether their silence means they took back their ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Have the רבנן taken back their ruling?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן asks his guests directly whether their silence means they now agree the סוכה is כשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is half friendly teasing and half a real challenge. If they slept there without complaining, it seems they must now hold the סוכה is valid. This sets up their answer.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: הֲדוּר בְּהוּ רַבָּנַן מִשְּׁמַעְתַּיְיהוּ?
phrases.english: He said to them: Have the Rabbis retracted their ruling?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from their silence in Step 9 and asks them to confirm it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether their silence means they now agree with רב נחמן that the סוכה is כשרה.

steps.title: They were exempt anyway as travelers on a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: They answer that they are שלוחי מצוה and exempt from סוכה, so their silence proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: We are people traveling for a מצוה, and we are exempt from the סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The guests explain that they did not change their opinion. Since they were traveling for a מצוה, they did not need a valid סוכה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone busy with one מצוה is exempt from another, so they had no obligation to sit in a כשרה סוכה. That is why they had no reason to object. Their ruling that the סוכה is פסולה stays exactly the same.

keyTerms.meaning: people on the way to do a מצוה

steps.whatToRemember: The argument from Step 8 is not settled by this story. רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא still hold the סוכה is פסולה; they were simply exempt.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read their silence as agreement. The story shows silence is not proof when the person had no obligation in the first place.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known source for the rule that שלוחי מצוה are exempt from סוכה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: אֲנַן שְׁלוּחֵי מִצְוָה אֲנַן,
phrases.english: They said to him: We are agents of a מצוה,
and we are exempt from the sukkah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's question by giving a different reason for their silence.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They did not retract; they were exempt from סוכה as שלוחי מצוה, so the סוכה's status did not matter to them.

steps.title: Sleeping under a low canopy inside the סוכה is allowed
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules you may sleep under a כילה in the סוכה even though it has a roof, as long as it is not ten טפחים high.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: It is permitted to sleep under a כילה inside the סוכה, even though it has a roof, as long as it is not ten טפחים high.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic. שמואל teaches that a canopy over a bed does not block you from the סוכה, as long as it is lower than ten טפחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally something with a roof between you and the סכך could cut you off from the סוכה. Below ten טפחים, the canopy does not count as its own tent (אהל), so you are still sleeping in the סוכה. The height is the deciding factor.

keyTerms.meaning: a canopy or netting over a bed
ten טפחים high, the minimum height to count as a tent

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
It is permitted to sleep under a canopy in the sukkah,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ גַּג,
phrases.english: even though it has a roof,
provided that it is not ten handbreadths high.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: מוּתָּר לִישַׁן בְּכִילָּה בַּסּוּכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a covering under the סכך that sits over the person, not over the whole סוכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כילה with a roof inside a סוכה is allowed to sleep under if it is less than ten טפחים high.

steps.title: A ברייתא says sleeping under a canopy does not count
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says one who sleeps under a כילה in the סוכה has not fulfilled his obligation, which seems to contradict שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One who sleeps under a כילה in the סוכה has not fulfilled his obligation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל with a ברייתא that seems to say the exact opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes no mention of height. It seems to say any כילה disqualifies, which goes against שמואל's permission.

keyTerms.meaning: he did not fulfill his obligation

phrases.english: Come and hear: One who sleeps under a canopy in the sukkah
has not fulfilled his obligation!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling from Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that sleeping under a כילה in the סוכה is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says without any condition that sleeping under a כילה does not fulfill the obligation, which directly contradicts שמואל.

steps.title: The ברייתא means a canopy ten handbreadths high
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a כילה that is ten טפחים high.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Where it is ten טפחים high.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is about a tall canopy, which שמואל also forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A canopy that is ten טפחים high counts as its own tent and separates the sleeper from the סוכה. A low one does not. So the ברייתא and שמואל agree; they are just describing different heights.

keyTerms.meaning: with what case are we dealing here (narrows a source to a specific case)

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
Where it is ten handbreadths high.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13 by limiting the ברייתא to a specific case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא forbids every כילה, no matter how high.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only forbids a כילה ten טפחים high, which fits with שמואל.

steps.title: The משנה says sleeping under a bed does not count
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says one who sleeps under a bed in the סוכה has not fulfilled his obligation, though beds are usually under ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a משנה: One who sleeps under the bed in the סוכה has not fulfilled his obligation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to שמואל, this time from a משנה about sleeping underneath a bed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ordinary bed is lower than ten טפחים. If sleeping under it still does not count, then even a low covering would seem to block you from the סוכה. That goes against שמואל's rule that height under ten does not matter.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: One who sleeps under the bed in the sukkah
has not fulfilled his obligation!
phrases.notes: This is a משנה (סוכה דף כ:).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, stronger challenge to שמואל, now from a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that a covering lower than ten טפחים does not separate you from the סוכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A normal bed is under ten טפחים, yet the משנה says sleeping under it does not count. So it seems a low covering does disqualify.

steps.title: שמואל already explained the משנה as a tall bed
steps.stepSummary: שמואל already explained that the משנה is about a bed ten טפחים high.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't שמואל already explain it as referring to a bed ten טפחים high?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל himself already explained this משנה as speaking about a bed ten טפחים high.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the bed in the משנה is ten טפחים high, it counts as its own tent, and that is why sleeping under it does not count. This fits perfectly with שמואל's rule. Both challenges are answered the same way: the height of ten טפחים is what matters.
steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, a covering under the סכך only separates you from the סוכה if it is ten טפחים high. Below that, you are still in the סוכה.

phrases.english: Didn't Shmuel already interpret it
as referring to a bed ten handbreadths high?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15 using שמואל's own explanation of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא), quoting the same אמורא's earlier explanation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about an ordinary bed, which is under ten טפחים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a bed ten טפחים high, so it fits with שמואל.

steps.title: A challenge from the canopy over four bed posts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה that spreading a sheet over קינופות makes the space under it פסולה, which seems to contradict שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'Or if he spread a sheet over the four bed posts, it is unfit!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another challenge to שמואל. It quotes our משנה, which says a sheet spread over four bed posts makes the space underneath פסולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bed posts are usually not ten טפחים high. Yet the משנה still says the area under the sheet is פסולה. That seems to show that a covering under ten טפחים does cut you off from the סוכה, which goes against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Four posts on the corners of a bed, used to hold up a canopy

phrases.english: Come and hear:
or if one spread a sheet over four bed posts —
it is unfit!
phrases.notes: The space under the sheet does not count as being in the סוכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another source is brought against שמואל, after the answers in Steps 14 and 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that a כילה under ten טפחים does not separate a person from the סוכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Bed posts are normally below ten, yet a canopy on them is פסולה, so a low covering does count.

steps.title: The posts in that case are ten טפחים high
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about posts that are ten טפחים high.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, it is a case where they are ten handbreadths high.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge the same way it did before. The משנה is talking about tall posts, ten טפחים high.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the posts are ten טפחים, the canopy is a real separate structure. Then the משנה fits שמואל's rule, which only allows a covering under ten.

phrases.english: There too,
it is where they are ten handbreadths high.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17 using the same approach as Steps 14 and 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to posts ten טפחים high
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to be talking about ordinary low bed posts.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is talking about posts ten טפחים high, so it does not contradict שמואל.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows four posts are פסולה even when low
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא makes a ten-טפחים condition only for two posts (נקליטין). This implies four posts (קינופות) are פסולה even under ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not how it was taught! For a ברייתא teaches: 'נקליטין are two posts, and קינופות are four posts. If one spread a sheet over קינופות, it is unfit. Over נקליטין, it is fit, as long as the נקליטין are not ten handbreadths higher than the bed.' This shows that קינופות are unfit even if they are not ten high!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the last answer. It quotes a ברייתא showing that four posts make the space פסולה even when they are not ten טפחים high.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds the 'not ten high' condition only for two posts. That means for four posts the height does not matter: they are פסולה either way. So the answer 'they are ten high' cannot explain the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: But that is not how it was taught
Two posts, one at the head and one at the foot of a bed, holding a cross-beam

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of posts. נקליטין are TWO posts with a sloping sheet, and they are fine if under ten. קינופות are FOUR posts with a flat canopy, and the ברייתא implies they are פסולה even when low.

phrases.english: But that is not how it was taught.
As it was taught in a ברייתא:
Naklitin are two posts,
and kinofot are four posts.
If one spread a sheet over the four posts — it is unfit;
over the two posts — it is fit,
as long as the two posts are not
ten handbreadths higher than the bed.
This shows that four posts make it unfit —

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין גְּבוֹהִין עֲשָׂרָה!
phrases.english: even if they are not ten handbreadths high!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the answer of Step 18 and brings back the challenge of Step 17 with more force.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה's קינופות are ten טפחים high
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives the 'not ten high' condition only for נקליטין. So for קינופות, height does not matter and they are פסולה even when low.

steps.title: Four posts are different because they are fixed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that קינופות are a special case because they are permanently fixed to the bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Four posts are different, because they are fixed in place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer. It agrees that four posts make the space פסולה even below ten, but explains this is because they are fixed and permanent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the reason is not height but permanence (קביעות). A fixed canopy counts as a real structure even when it is low. A regular כילה is not fixed, so שמואל's rule still applies to it.

phrases.english: Four posts are different,
because they are fixed in place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed height answer (Step 18) with a new reason: permanence.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: a fixed structure versus a movable one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any covering under ten טפחים should not separate a person from the סוכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A fixed covering like קינופות counts as separate even under ten. שמואל's rule is about a movable כילה.

steps.title: But a סוכה on top of a סוכה is fixed and still needs ten
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the 'fixed' answer: a סוכה על גבי סוכה is fixed, yet שמואל says it only disqualifies the lower one at ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a סוכה on top of another סוכה is fixed, and yet שמואל said: just as its fitness needs ten, so does its power to disqualify!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer about fixed posts. It points to the case of a סוכה built on top of a סוכה, which is also fixed but still needs ten טפחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said the upper סוכה makes the lower one פסולה only if it is ten טפחים, the same height it needs to be kosher itself. That case is fixed too. So being fixed does not seem to remove the need for ten.

keyTerms.meaning: A סוכה built on top of another סוכה
As its fitness, so is its unfitness: the same height rule (ten) applies to both
But look at / but here is

phrases.english: But a sukka on top of another sukka
is fixed,
and Shmuel said:
as is its fitness, so is its unfitness!
phrases.notes: The upper סוכה needs ten טפחים to be kosher, and it also needs ten to disqualify the lower one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי סוּכָּה עַל גַּבֵּי סוּכָּה דִּקְבִיעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'fixed' answer of Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a fixed covering counts as separate even under ten טפחים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A סוכה על גבי סוכה is fixed, yet שמואל requires ten for it to disqualify. So being fixed should not be enough.

steps.title: Disqualifying a סוכה needs ten; making a tent does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא separates two questions: turning the upper structure into a סוכה that disqualifies the lower one needs ten. Simply making a tent over a person can happen below ten when it is fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: There, where the question is disqualifying the סוכה, ten is needed. Here, where the question is making it a tent, even less than ten counts as a tent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two cases ask different questions. One is about disqualifying a סוכה, and the other is about whether something counts as a tent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a סוכה על גבי סוכה, the upper one disqualifies the lower only if it is a real dwelling of its own, which needs ten. With קינופות, we only ask whether the canopy forms an אוהל between the person and the סכך. A fixed canopy is an אוהל even below ten.

keyTerms.meaning: To make it count as a tent

steps.whatToRemember: A movable כילה under ten does not cut you off from the סוכה (שמואל). Fixed קינופות count as an אוהל even under ten. Ten טפחים is required only when the question is whether one structure disqualifies a סוכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the גמרא using one height number (ten) for different legal jobs. The rule depends on the question being asked: making a separate dwelling, or simply forming a tent.

phrases.english: They say:
There, where it is to disqualify a sukka — ten is needed.
Here, where it is to make it a tent —
even less than ten is also a tent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 21 and saves the 'fixed' answer of Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separating two different legal functions (disqualifying a סוכה versus forming an אוהל)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any fixed structure should follow the same ten-טפחים rule as a סוכה על גבי סוכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Ten is needed only to disqualify a סוכה. A fixed covering forms an אוהל even below ten.

steps.title: Reciting קריאת שמע while sleeping unclothed under a כילה
steps.stepSummary: רב תחליפא בר אבימי quotes שמואל: a person sleeping unclothed under a כילה may put his head outside it and recite קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב תחליפא בר אבימי said in the name of שמואל: One who sleeps unclothed under a כילה puts his head outside the כילה and recites קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling of שמואל about a כילה, this time about קריאת שמע. A person lying unclothed under a כילה may put his head out of it and say שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person may not recite קריאת שמע while his body is uncovered. Here the כילה acts as a separating covering, so his head outside is treated as separated from his uncovered body. The sugya is still exploring how significant a כילה is.

keyTerms.meaning: A canopy or netting over a bed

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר אֲבִימִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Taḥalifa bar Avimi said that Shmuel said:
One who sleeps unclothed under a canopy-netting —
puts his head outside the netting
and recites Shema.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר אֲבִימִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement of שמואל about the status of a כילה, now in the area of קריאת שמע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person lying unclothed under a כילה may put his head outside it and recite קריאת שמע, because the כילה acts as a separating covering.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to forbid what שמואל allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא saying a person sleeping unclothed under a כילה may NOT put his head out and say קריאת שמע. This contradicts שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: one who sleeps unclothed under a כילה may not put his head outside the כילה and recite קריאת שמע!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the exact opposite of what שמואל just said. This is an attack on שמואל's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל allowed the person to stick his head out and say קריאת שמע. The ברייתא describes the same case and forbids it. So the גמרא asks how שמואל can rule against a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: He may not put his head out

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who sleeps unclothed under a canopy-net
may not put his head outside the net
phrases.notes: This is the exact case of שמואל, with the opposite ruling.

phrases.english: and recite the Shema!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges שמואל's ruling quoted in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that one may put his head outside the כילה and recite קריאת שמע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא rules on the identical case and forbids it, so שמואל contradicts a תנאי source.

steps.title: The ברייתא speaks of a כילה ten טפחים high
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a כילה that is ten טפחים tall. שמואל was talking about a lower one.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here? A case where the כילה is ten טפחים high.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל. It says the ברייתא and שמואל are talking about two different kinds of כילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כילה ten טפחים high counts as a tent, a separate space. The person's unclothed body is inside that space, so putting his head out does not help. A lower כילה is more like a garment covering him, so putting his head out works, as שמואל said.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the height makes the person more covered. It is the reverse: a tall כילה is a separate tent, and his uncovered body is inside it, so it does not count as covering him.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
When it is ten handbreadths high.
phrases.notes: Ten טפחים makes it a tent, like the tall כילה in steps 12-14.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 24 by limiting the ברייתא to a specific case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא refers only to a כילה ten טפחים high.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא forbids it in every case, which contradicts שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא forbids it only when the כילה is ten טפחים high and counts as a tent. שמואל permits it when the כילה is lower.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא compares it to a house, which supports the answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that this reading makes sense. The ברייתא's own second half compares the case to a person in a house who puts his head out a window.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too it makes sense, since the end of the ברייתא teaches: To what is this similar? To someone standing unclothed in a house, who may not put his head out the window and recite קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support from the ברייתא itself for its answer that the כילה is ten טפחים high.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא compares the כילה to a house. Only a tall כילה, ten טפחים, is a real tent like a house. So the comparison shows that the ברייתא was talking about a ten-טפחים כילה all along.

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
since it teaches in the latter clause:
To what is this comparable?
To one standing unclothed in a house,
who may not put his head out the window
phrases.notes: A house is clearly a tent, so the כילה must be ten טפחים to be compared to it.

phrases.english: and recite the Shema.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 25 from the wording of the same ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the ברייתא refers to a כילה ten טפחים high
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the ברייתא, which compares the case to a person in a house putting his head out a window

steps.title: Conclusion: the reading is proven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the proof works. The ברייתא speaks of a ten-טפחים כילה, and שמואל's ruling stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion. It accepts the proof from the end of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the two sources fit together. A כילה ten טפחים high is like a house, and putting your head out does not help. A lower כילה is like a garment, and putting your head out works, as שמואל said.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it (the proof is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: Height decides it. A כילה ten טפחים high is a tent, like a house, so putting your head out does not allow קריאת שמע. A lower כילה is like a garment, so שמואל permits it.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the proof brought in step 26.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא refers to a כילה ten טפחים high, which counts as a tent. שמואל's permission applies to a lower כילה.
